summary: The health-tech investment landscape remains robust, with significant capital flowing into medical device innovation and healthcare operations. Medical Microinstruments raised $125 million for its robotic microsurgery platform and Alzheimer's research, while rare disease biotech Setara launched with $90 million to develop treatments for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and overactive bladder, and Midstream Health secured $20 million to help health systems improve financial stability. On the technology front, AI-driven health tools are facing increased regulatory scrutiny, with Australia's TGA signaling that popular AI scribes may require medical device classification, while major tech players are expanding healthcare capabilities through new partnerships—Oracle and AstraZeneca are collaborating on clinical trial optimization, and NVIDIA is launching healthcare AI and protein design initiatives. In surgical innovation, Phantom Neuro has begun human implants of its muscle-machine interface technology, marking another milestone in neurotechnology development.
